subject: Model shortlist, context lanes & ramp — kickoff questions
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@novalabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: eng+prod@novalabs.com
Date: 2027-09-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Initial sizing info + shortlist ask

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to lock a short list of candidate models and get a sizing snapshot before the kickoff next week. A few specifics from our side:

- Primary use: contextual answer generation from internal docs (median prompt ~120 tokens, average response ~220 tokens).
- Expected first-month traffic: ~150k requests (mix of single-turn and short multi-turn flows) with 5% peak concurrency on afternoon spikes.
- Latency target: p95 < 600ms for interactive UI flows.

Can you and your CS/implementation team propose 2–3 model candidates (one latency-first, one cost-first, one quality-first) and a rough token estimate and instance sizing per model? Also, we attached a 48h sample of our traffic and a short CSV of request timestamps.

Attachments: novalabs-sample-traffic.csv (csv, 85KB)

—Ari
Ari Kaplan
Head of Product, Nova Labs
ari@novalabs.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@novalabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing info + shortlist ask

Ari — thanks for the traffic sample, that helps. Im looping in Monica (CS lead) and Grace (modeling) to prepare a concise shortlist and a quick run-of-show for kickoff. High-level plan from our side:

1) Well produce 3 candidates:
   - Latency-first: distilled / quantized variant (low token cost, smaller window, best for p95 latency)
   - Cost-first: smaller Llama-family trimmed and quantized (best unit economics for high QPS)
   - Quality-first: full FP16/gpt-style open model (higher cost, larger context)

2) For each candidate well provide: expected tokens/request, instance footprint, two ramp profiles (pilot -> 3mo) and a short risk table (context truncation, hallucination sensitivity).

3) Proposed kickoff deliverables: model shortlist + token projection spreadsheet, a basic inference configuration (batching, cache policy), and a runbook for a 2-week pilot. Im attaching a short evaluation summary were preparing — Monica will add token worksheets.

Next steps: Monica will send a more detailed token-profile and a few clarifying Qs. Would you prefer an hour kickoff Wed 09/29 or Thu 09/30?

Attachments: novalabs-eval-summary.pdf (pdf, 450KB)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@novalabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing info + shortlist ask — token questions and draft projections

Ari / team — quick follow-up from CS and modeling after looking at the sample:

Summary assumptions (confirm if these are correct):
- Median prompt length: 120 tokens (you noted this)
- Median response length assumption for planning: 220 tokens (we'll model 200/220/350 for sensitivity)
- Average metadata/context per request (prefix + doc snippets cached): ~80 tokens

Questions:
- Peak concurrency: when you say 5% peak concurrency, is that 5% of daily requests concentrated into a 5–10 minute window (we need the spike duration for batching policy)?
- SLA tolerance: do you require p95 < 600ms on the pilot or after Dedicated procurement?
- Any hard constraints on model size (e.g., cannot exceed 40B params for governance)?

Draft projections (very rough):
- Latency-first candidate (quantized 13B variant): ~380 tokens/request on average -> ~57M tokens/month; one dedicated 4xA10-style pool (or 2xA100 high-mem) for headroom at pilot; cost-optimised batching + prefix cache.
- Cost-first candidate (8–10B quantized): ~360 tokens/request -> ~54M tokens/month; can start on shared hosted with autoscale for initial month.
- Quality-first candidate (35–40B FP16): ~420 tokens/request -> ~63M tokens/month; expected higher peak memory, plan for Dedicated or high-vCPU+GPU nodes.

Attachments: token_profile_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB)

Ask: if you can confirm spike shape and any governance limits today well finalize the matrix and a recommended pilot config. If Wed 09/29 works for you, well use that call to finalize the shortlist and lock the pilot scope.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ari Kaplan <ari@novalabs.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing info + shortlist ask — infra note

Quick ops note from infra:

- The estimated token ranges look reasonable. For the quality-first candidate well need to reserve GPUs with ~80–100GB effective memory for the KV/cache + model footprint if you want FP16 without sharding. If Nova prefers lower hardware cost, we can explore 4-bit quantized variants but expect some quality delta.
- For pilot stability I recommend: 2-week smoke on hosted with warm prefix cache, then move to a 1-month Dedicated pool if telemetry (p95, error-rate, token burn) meets thresholds.
- Ill draft a technical appendix for the kickoff that maps model -> recommended instance types and expected concurrency headroom. Attaching a quick draft of the Dedicated plan for reference.

Attachments: dedicated-plan-draft.md (md, 6KB)

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior SW Eng — Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference
